name: ANSI cross-coupled NAND latch
summary: Two NAND gates with outputs fed back to each other, forming an SR latch with active-low set and reset.
description: Drawing the latch as two cross-coupled NAND gates shows its construction explicitly. A low on the set input forces Q high; a low on the reset input forces the complement high. With both inputs high the latch holds. Both inputs low drives both outputs high, which is normally treated as invalid.

This drawing form is common in teaching material, switch debounce circuits and older schematics where the latch is built from a quad NAND package. It lets a reviewer see the feedback paths and the pins used.
Because the latch is built from gates, the drawing shows nothing about which state it adopts at power-up. If a defined state is needed, a reset pulse or a pull network must be shown.
readingNotes: Both inputs low gives both outputs high and is usually avoided.
drawingChecklist: Draw the feedback paths clearly without ambiguous crossings.
Mark inputs as active low in the net names.
distinction: The cross-coupled NOR latch has active-high inputs.
